blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Solve the following system of linear equations by Cramer's rule: \(2x + y - z = 1\), \(x - y + 2z = 3\), \(3x + 2y + z = 4\)
blocks.explanation:
Three equations in three unknowns, to be solved with determinants (Cramer's rule).
We must find all three unknowns.
Plan: find \(|A|\); then the three determinants with one column replaced by the constants; divide; check.
steps:
Given: \(2x + y - z = 1\), \(x - y + 2z = 3\), \(3x + 2y + z = 4\)
To find: \(x, y, z\) by Cramer's rule.
Method: Write \(AX = B\). If \(|A| \neq 0\), then \(x = \dfrac{|A_{x}|}{|A|}\), \(y = \dfrac{|A_{y}|}{|A|}\), \(z = \dfrac{|A_{z}|}{|A|}\), where \(|A_{x}|\) is \(|A|\) with column 1 replaced by the constants \(B\), and so on.

Write the coefficient matrix and constants
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]
\[B = \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Row \(k\) of \(A\) holds the coefficients of \(x, y, z\) in equation \(k\); a missing variable has coefficient 0.

Find \(|A|\) (expand along \(R_1\))
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 2(-1 - 4) - 1(1 - 6) - 1(2 + 3)\]
\[= -10 + 5 - 5\]
\[= -10\]
Why: \(|A| \neq 0\), so Cramer's rule applies and the solution is unique.

Find \(|A_{x}|\): replace column 1 by \(B\)
\[|A_{x}| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-1 - 4) - 1(3 - 8) - 1(6 + 4)\]
\[= -5 + 5 - 10\]
\[= -10\]
Why: For \(x\) the first column (coefficients of \(x\)) is replaced by the constants.

Find \(|A_{y}|\): replace column 2 by \(B\)
\[|A_{y}| = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 2(3 - 8) - 1(1 - 6) - 1(4 - 9)\]
\[= -10 + 5 + 5\]
\[= 0\]
Why: For \(y\) the second column (coefficients of \(y\)) is replaced by the constants.

Find \(|A_{z}|\): replace column 3 by \(B\)
\[|A_{z}| = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & 4\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 2(-4 - 6) - 1(4 - 9) + 1(2 + 3)\]
\[= -20 + 5 + 5\]
\[= -10\]
Why: For \(z\) the third column (coefficients of \(z\)) is replaced by the constants.

Apply Cramer's rule
\[x = \dfrac{|A_{x}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{-10}{-10} = 1\]
\[y = \dfrac{|A_{y}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{0}{-10} = 0\]
\[z = \dfrac{|A_{z}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{-10}{-10} = 1\]
Why: Each unknown is its own determinant divided by \(|A|\). Simplify the fraction and keep the sign.

Check in all three equations
\[2(1) + (0) - (1) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
\[(1) - (0) + 2(1) = 3 \;\checkmark\]
\[3(1) + 2(0) + (1) = 4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The values satisfy every equation, so the solution is correct.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Solve the following system of linear equations by Cramer's rule: \(x_1 + 2x_2 - 3x_3 = 0\), \(4x_1 - x_2 + x_3 = 5\), \(-2x_1 + 3x_2 + 2x_3 = 3\)
blocks.explanation:
Three equations in three unknowns, to be solved with determinants (Cramer's rule).
We must find all three unknowns.
Plan: find \(|A|\); then the three determinants with one column replaced by the constants; divide; check.
steps:
Given: \(x_1 + 2x_2 - 3x_3 = 0\), \(4x_1 - x_2 + x_3 = 5\), \(-2x_1 + 3x_2 + 2x_3 = 3\)
To find: \(x_1, x_2, x_3\) by Cramer's rule.
Method: Write \(AX = B\). If \(|A| \neq 0\), then \(x_1 = \dfrac{|A_{x_1}|}{|A|}\), \(x_2 = \dfrac{|A_{x_2}|}{|A|}\), \(x_3 = \dfrac{|A_{x_3}|}{|A|}\), where \(|A_{x_1}|\) is \(|A|\) with column 1 replaced by the constants \(B\), and so on.

Write the coefficient matrix and constants
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
\[B = \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Row \(k\) of \(A\) holds the coefficients of \(x_1, x_2, x_3\) in equation \(k\); a missing variable has coefficient 0.

Find \(|A|\) (expand along \(R_1\))
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-2 - 3) - 2(8 + 2) - 3(12 - 2)\]
\[= -5 - 20 - 30\]
\[= -55\]
Why: \(|A| \neq 0\), so Cramer's rule applies and the solution is unique.

Find \(|A_{x_1}|\): replace column 1 by \(B\)
\[|A_{x_1}| = \begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 & -3 \\ 5 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 0(-2 - 3) - 2(10 - 3) - 3(15 + 3)\]
\[= 0 - 14 - 54\]
\[= -68\]
Why: For \(x_1\) the first column (coefficients of \(x_1\)) is replaced by the constants.

Find \(|A_{x_2}|\): replace column 2 by \(B\)
\[|A_{x_2}| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 \\ 4 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(10 - 3) + 0(8 + 2) - 3(12 + 10)\]
\[= 7 + 0 - 66\]
\[= -59\]
Why: For \(x_2\) the second column (coefficients of \(x_2\)) is replaced by the constants.

Find \(|A_{x_3}|\): replace column 3 by \(B\)
\[|A_{x_3}| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 5 \\ -2 & 3 & 3\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-3 - 15) - 2(12 + 10) + 0(12 - 2)\]
\[= -18 - 44 + 0\]
\[= -62\]
Why: For \(x_3\) the third column (coefficients of \(x_3\)) is replaced by the constants.

Apply Cramer's rule
\[x_1 = \dfrac{|A_{x_1}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{-68}{-55} = \dfrac{68}{55}\]
\[x_2 = \dfrac{|A_{x_2}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{-59}{-55} = \dfrac{59}{55}\]
\[x_3 = \dfrac{|A_{x_3}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{-62}{-55} = \dfrac{62}{55}\]
Why: Each unknown is its own determinant divided by \(|A|\). Simplify the fraction and keep the sign.

Check in all three equations
\[\left(\frac{68}{55}\right) + 2\left(\frac{59}{55}\right) - 3\left(\frac{62}{55}\right) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[4\left(\frac{68}{55}\right) - \left(\frac{59}{55}\right) + \left(\frac{62}{55}\right) = 5 \;\checkmark\]
\[-2\left(\frac{68}{55}\right) + 3\left(\frac{59}{55}\right) + 2\left(\frac{62}{55}\right) = 3 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The values satisfy every equation, so the solution is correct.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) Solve the following system of linear equations by Cramer's rule: \(2x_1 - x_2 + x_3 = 1\), \(x_1 + 2x_2 + 2x_3 = 2\), \(x_1 - 2x_2 - x_3 = 1\)
blocks.explanation:
Three equations in three unknowns, to be solved with determinants (Cramer's rule).
We must find all three unknowns.
Plan: find \(|A|\); then the three determinants with one column replaced by the constants; divide; check.
steps:
Given: \(2x_1 - x_2 + x_3 = 1\), \(x_1 + 2x_2 + 2x_3 = 2\), \(x_1 - 2x_2 - x_3 = 1\)
To find: \(x_1, x_2, x_3\) by Cramer's rule.
Method: Write \(AX = B\). If \(|A| \neq 0\), then \(x_1 = \dfrac{|A_{x_1}|}{|A|}\), \(x_2 = \dfrac{|A_{x_2}|}{|A|}\), \(x_3 = \dfrac{|A_{x_3}|}{|A|}\), where \(|A_{x_1}|\) is \(|A|\) with column 1 replaced by the constants \(B\), and so on.

Write the coefficient matrix and constants
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\]
\[B = \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Row \(k\) of \(A\) holds the coefficients of \(x_1, x_2, x_3\) in equation \(k\); a missing variable has coefficient 0.

Find \(|A|\) (expand along \(R_1\))
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 2(-2 + 4) + 1(-1 - 2) + 1(-2 - 2)\]
\[= 4 - 3 - 4\]
\[= -3\]
Why: \(|A| \neq 0\), so Cramer's rule applies and the solution is unique.

Find \(|A_{x_1}|\): replace column 1 by \(B\)
\[|A_{x_1}| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-2 + 4) + 1(-2 - 2) + 1(-4 - 2)\]
\[= 2 - 4 - 6\]
\[= -8\]
Why: For \(x_1\) the first column (coefficients of \(x_1\)) is replaced by the constants.

Find \(|A_{x_2}|\): replace column 2 by \(B\)
\[|A_{x_2}| = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 2(-2 - 2) - 1(-1 - 2) + 1(1 - 2)\]
\[= -8 + 3 - 1\]
\[= -6\]
Why: For \(x_2\) the second column (coefficients of \(x_2\)) is replaced by the constants.

Find \(|A_{x_3}|\): replace column 3 by \(B\)
\[|A_{x_3}| = \begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 2(2 + 4) + 1(1 - 2) + 1(-2 - 2)\]
\[= 12 - 1 - 4\]
\[= 7\]
Why: For \(x_3\) the third column (coefficients of \(x_3\)) is replaced by the constants.

Apply Cramer's rule
\[x_1 = \dfrac{|A_{x_1}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{-8}{-3} = \dfrac{8}{3}\]
\[x_2 = \dfrac{|A_{x_2}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{-6}{-3} = 2\]
\[x_3 = \dfrac{|A_{x_3}|}{|A|} = \dfrac{7}{-3} = -\dfrac{7}{3}\]
Why: Each unknown is its own determinant divided by \(|A|\). Simplify the fraction and keep the sign.

Check in all three equations
\[2\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) - (2) + \left(-\frac{7}{3}\right) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
\[\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) + 2(2) + 2\left(-\frac{7}{3}\right) = 2 \;\checkmark\]
\[\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) - 2(2) - \left(-\frac{7}{3}\right) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The values satisfy every equation, so the solution is correct.
